description: “I made a ScratchJr story about growing food on the Moon. My astronaut builds a greenhouse, waters the plants and grows strawberries in space!”
summary: I made an animated story in ScratchJr called Growing Food on the Moon. My astronaut flies to the Moon by rocket with a robot friend. On the Moon, I build a greenhouse to grow plants, then water them until strawberries grow. At the end, the rocket flies back to Earth. I recorded my own voice to tell the story, and I used block coding to make the characters move and to change pages. My project shows how astronauts could grow their own food in space one day.
details:
What does it do / how does it work?
My project is an animated story called Growing Food on the Moon. It has 4 pages. An astronaut lands on the Moon with a robot friend, builds a greenhouse, waters the plants until strawberries grow, and then flies back to Earth. When you tap a character, it plays a sound, says my recorded voice, moves, and goes to the next page.

What benefits does it have?
It teaches how astronauts could grow their own food in space. It also helped me practise coding, storytelling and speaking.

What is the intended impact?
I want other children to think about how people could live on the Moon one day, and to see that they can tell their own stories with code.

What tools did you use?
I used ScratchJr on an iPad. I used block coding: sound blocks, voice recording blocks, motion blocks (move up and back) and “go to page” blocks to connect the pages. I drew my own robot, greenhouse, plants and watering can in the paint editor, and I added my own photo to the astronaut.

How is it creative?
I turned a real science idea, farming in space, into a story. I drew my own characters, put myself in the story as the astronaut, and told the story in my own voice.

What factors did I consider?

  • Story order: The pages had to make sense from start to end.
  • Plants’ needs: I thought about what plants need to grow on the Moon, like a greenhouse and water.
  • Blocks: I put the blocks in the right order so each character moves and changes the page.
  • Clear voice: I recorded my voice clearly so everyone can understand the story.
